name: Crunch
description: The crunch is a foundational abdominal exercise that trains the rectus abdominis through a short-range trunk flexion movement. Unlike the sit-up, the crunch limits the range of motion to protect the lumbar spine, keeping the lower back on the floor and moving only the upper back and shoulders off the ground.

execution.starting_position: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place hands lightly behind the head or crossed on the chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Keep the lower back in contact with the floor throughout. The movement range is short — only the upper back and shoulders come off the floor.
steps: Breathe out and curl the shoulders and upper back off the floor toward the knees.
Hold the top position briefly, squeezing the abdominals.
Lower under control back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you crunch up. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Pulling the neck with the hands
Using momentum by bouncing the head up
Raising the lower back off the floor
safety_considerations: If neck pain occurs, cross arms on chest instead of placing hands behind the head
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Upper back and shoulders come 2–4 inches off the floor. Lower back remains in contact with the floor.
coaching_cues: Think about bringing your ribcage toward your pelvis — not your head toward your knees
Keep your neck neutral — do not lead with the chin
